name: Golgi apparatus
short_description: The cell's packing and dispatch station: a polarised stack of four to eight smooth, flattened membrane sacs that takes freshly built proteins in on its convex cis face, tags them with sugar chains, sorts them, and pinches them off the concave trans face in vesicles addressed to the cell surface, to lysosomes or to export.

textbook.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the science is broadly right - five separate flattened cisternae, an amber-to-violet cis-to-trans colour gradient, an orange lacy cis-Golgi network under the bottom sac, an indigo trans-Golgi network and budding secretory vesicles above, a ribosome-studded rough-ER ribbon at the lower left contrasted against perfectly smooth Golgi membranes, muted palette, thin outlines, dark charcoal ground, no text and no border - but the stack is drawn FLAT: the cis face is not convex and the trans face is not concave, so the organelle's defining polarity is carried only by colour and by the attached networks, not by its shape. The cisternal rims are also tapered rather than dilated. Fix-prompt: bow the whole stack like a shallow smile so the bottom sac bulges downward (convex cis) and the top sac is cupped upward (concave trans); make each sac an extremely thin sheet whose two ends swell into small rounded knobs)
textbook.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the bowl geometry landed - the stack is now clearly bowed with a convex amber cis face below and a concave violet trans face cupped above - and every other element is correct and cleanly separated, but the COPI vesicles budding at the rims are arranged as a perfectly bilaterally symmetric row of identical 'lollipops' flanking both sides of the stack, which reads as decoration rather than biology, and the rims are still not visibly dilated. Fix-prompt: escalate the model; keep the bow, scatter the rim vesicles irregularly, and give each cisterna a genuinely swollen rim)
textbook.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; five clearly separate flattened cisternae bowed into a shallow bowl, each with a pale cream lumen and distinctly swollen teardrop rims pierced by sparse irregular fenestration slits. The convex amber-orange cis face sits at the bottom with an elaborate lacy orange cis-Golgi network hanging beneath it; the medial cisternae shift through orange, coral and dusty rose; the concave mauve-violet trans face is cupped upward and its hollow opens into a branching indigo trans-Golgi network from which pale-blue cargo-filled secretory vesicles bud, one still on a neck, plus a bristly clathrin-coated vesicle at the right. A grey-blue rough-ER ribbon studded with ribosome dots enters at the lower left with mint COPII vesicles and a green ERGIC cluster; mustard COPI vesicles sit at the rims and lilac peripheral tubules trail sideways. Golgi membranes are completely smooth - no ribosomes, no bead rows. Muted educational palette with thin coloured outlines on a neutral dark charcoal ground, edge to edge, no text, no arrows, no border, no frame)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; a false-colour deep-etch/freeze-fracture style micrograph of a single Golgi stack seen at a three-quarter angle - seven separate flattened disc-shaped cisternae with a visible gap of cytoplasm between each pair, rims swelling into rounded bulges and drawn out into fine tubules, a warm amber cis face at the bottom carrying a lacy orange tubular network and vesicle cluster, grading through terracotta in the medial cisternae to muted violet at the top, and a dense dusty-indigo cloud of budding vesicles filling the trans side. A rough-ER fragment enters at the lower left with its surface clearly studded with ribosome particles while every Golgi membrane stays smooth - the key diagnostic contrast. Shallow depth of field, cool microscopy lighting, dark uncluttered charcoal background, single specimen, no cristae, no nuclear pores, no text, no scale bar, no border. Honest caveat: the cisternae are modelled thicker than the true ~10-20 nm lumen, and the stack is not visibly bowed - a legibility compromise, not an error of identity)

3d.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; six lens-shaped cisternae in a flat, unbowed pile with the cis/trans colour gradient present but the geometry wrong, edges rendered as an eyelash-like fringe of fine filaments rather than tubulated rims, and a few small dark dots sitting directly on the cisternal membranes that could be misread as ribosomes. Fix-prompt: bow the stack into a bowl, make the sacs paper-thin sheets rather than lenses, remove the hairy fringe, keep every membrane unbeaded)
3d.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a clear regression. The stack went flatter still, the entire edge of every cisterna sprouted a dense fringe of hairs and bristles that reads as cilia, and rows of pale beads appeared along the rims - the exact rough-ER confusion the reference forbids. The colour gradient also collapsed to warm cream and orange, losing the violet and indigo end. Escalated to gemini-3-pro-image)
3d.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; six clearly separate, thin flattened cisternae bowed into a shallow bowl, each with a bright cream luminal stripe and dilated rounded teardrop rims carrying sparse fenestration slits. The convex amber cis face at the bottom opens into an elaborate orange lacy cis-Golgi network; the medial cisternae run orange, terracotta and dusty rose; the concave violet trans face is cupped upward with a branching indigo trans-Golgi network above it, off which pale translucent blue secretory vesicles bud - one caught mid-pinch on a thin neck - alongside dark slate clathrin-coated vesicles. Grey-blue rough-ER ribbons studded with ribosome beads occupy the lower left with mint COPII vesicles and a sea-green ERGIC cluster; mustard COPI vesicles sit in the inter-cisternal gaps. Natural believable biological tints spanning the full cis-to-trans range - not near-monochrome, not neon - soft global illumination, subsurface scattering, clean dark studio ground, edge to edge, single specimen, no cristae, no nuclear pores, no hairs, no bead rows on any Golgi membrane, no text, no border. Minor note: the composition is almost perfectly bilaterally symmetric, which is tidier than a real stack)

watercolor.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed warm aged paper with a soft wash halo, correct violet-to-amber gradient and a stack of six separate cisternae with cream lumina - but the stack is flat rather than bowed, and rows of small circles run along every cisternal membrane, which reads as ribosomes studding the Golgi and is the single most misleading thing this organelle can be drawn with. Fix-prompt: bow the stack into a bowl and keep every Golgi membrane line clean and unbeaded)
watercolor.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the bow arrived and the paper is still full-bleed, but the colour gradient collapsed to an almost monochrome cream-and-orange stack, losing the violet and indigo trans end entirely, and the sacs nested into one another so tightly that they read as a stack of croissants rather than separate compartments. Escalated to gemini-3-pro-image)
watercolor.3: partial (gemini-3-pro-image; a genuinely beautiful plate - full-bleed aged paper corner to corner with a soft grey wash halo, no mat, frame, drop shadow or sheet-on-a-surface; the stack bowed correctly with a convex amber cis face and its lacy perforated cis-Golgi network below, a full amber-coral-mauve-violet gradient, a branching indigo trans-Golgi network and blue cargo-filled secretory vesicles above, a stippled rough-ER ribbon at the lower left. Rejected on one specific rule: two small directional ARROWS are painted beside the arriving COPII vesicles, and the house rules forbid any baked-in arrow. Fix-prompt: identical scene, absolutely no arrowheads or pointers of any kind)
watercolor.4: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; the same composition with the arrows gone. Warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner with a soft grey wash halo painted directly on it - no mat, no border, no frame, no drop shadow, no sheet lying on a surface. Six bowed, individually outlined cisternae with pale cream lumina and swollen rounded rims, the full cis-to-trans gradient from a convex amber cis face at the bottom (with its lacy perforated orange cis-Golgi network beneath) through coral and dusty rose to a concave mauve-violet trans face whose hollow opens into a branching indigo trans-Golgi network shedding blue cargo-filled secretory vesicles. Grey-blue rough-ER ribbon finely stippled with ink ribosome dots at the lower left, bright green COPII vesicles, a teal ERGIC blob, yellow COPI specks at the rims, lilac peripheral tubules trailing sideways. Every Golgi membrane is unbeaded and smooth. Fine ink linework over translucent washes, no text, no arrows, no scale bar. Honest caveat: the cisternae are painted plumper and more tubular than the true near-flat geometry - the same legibility compromise the printed atlases make)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Human leukocyte, showing golgi - TEM.jpg", Public domain, Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College, JEOL 100CX TEM. A genuine thin-section transmission electron micrograph of a human white blood cell in which a Golgi apparatus is unmistakable: a stack of six or seven closely apposed dark parallel membrane lines bowed into a shallow crescent across the lower half of the frame, the ends of the lines swelling into the characteristic rounded dilated-rim profiles, with the concave side of the arc facing up and crowded with a dense cloud of round and elongated vesicle profiles - the trans-face vesicle field - and the convex cis side facing down and outward, so the cis/trans polarity is directly readable. The membranes carry none of the ribosome studding that would mark rough ER. Cleaned in two edit_image.py passes: the white caption bar ("3Blood Cells … REMF"), all instrument data and the white letterbox bands were removed, the picture now bleeds to all four edges, and a restrained natural false-colour was applied following the same cis-to-trans convention as the rendered plates. Honest caveat: the second pass was asked to zoom in and recentre the stack and largely declined - the cleaned image keeps the original framing, so the left end of the crescent still runs off the left edge and the stack sits low rather than centred. Nothing was invented, sharpened or added)
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; attempts 1 and 2 on gemini-2.5-flash-image failed on the flat, unbowed stack and on decorative bilaterally-symmetric rim vesicles, and gemini-3-pro-image delivered the correct convex-cis / concave-trans bowl with dilated fenestrated rims on the first try

use as final; labelled figure built. Attempts 1 and 2 on gemini-2.5-flash-image were rejected for a flat stack, an eyelash-like fringe on every cisternal edge and bead rows along the rims that read as ribosomes; gemini-3-pro-image fixed all three and gave natural, clearly distinguishable biological tints across the full cis-to-trans range

use as final on the first attempt; correct false-colour surface-only view of a single stack with the diagnostic smooth-Golgi-versus-studded-rough-ER contrast. Not labelled (SEM is the surface-only comparison plate). Cisternae are modelled thicker than life and the stack is not bowed - a knowingly accepted legibility compromise

use as final; labelled figure built with black-on-paper ink. Attempts 1 and 2 on gemini-2.5-flash-image failed on beaded membranes and on a collapsed colour gradient; attempt 3 on gemini-3-pro-image was rejected solely for two baked-in directional arrows, and attempt 4 is the same composition without them. Cisternae are painted plumper than the true near-flat geometry
